title: Generator opens and homogeneous-fraction chart data for a graded line-module map
statement: Let $f:W\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ be a quasi-coherent commutative graded $\mathcal O_T$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures], and let $L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_W$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Use the tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and tensor powers [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Given degreewise module morphisms $\psi_n:f^*\mathcal A_n\to L^{\otimes n}$, define the image of $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal A_n)$ to be $\psi_n(1\otimes a)\in\Gamma(f^{-1}V,L^{\otimes n})$. For affine $V\subseteq T$, view $a$ as the corresponding homogeneous element of degree $n$ in $C_V=\Gamma(V,\mathcal A)$, with the section grading used by relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For a section $e$ of $L$ on an open $U\subseteq W$, define $e^{\otimes0}=1$ and $e^{\otimes(n+1)}=e\otimes e^{\otimes n}$. For affine $V$, $d\geq0$ and $a\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal A_d)$, define $U_a\subseteq f^{-1}V$ as the generating locus of $\psi_d(1\otimes a)$ [def-sc-section-generating-locus], regarded as an open of $W$. For any open $U\subseteq W$, commutative ring $R$, and morphism $r:U\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, define its scalar map $R\to\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_W)$ as the map on global sections composed with the canonical affine-spectrum and open-restriction identifications. A fraction chart at $(V,d,a)$ means a scheme morphism $r:U_a\to\operatorname{Spec}(C_{V,(a),0})$, where $C_{V,(a),0}$ is degree-zero homogeneous localization [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero]. More generally, for an open $U\subseteq f^{-1}V$ and a morphism $r:U\to\operatorname{Spec}(C_{V,(a),0})$, its homogeneous-fraction formula is the predicate that for every $m\geq0$ and $b\in\Gamma(V,\mathcal A_{md})$ the scalar image of $b/a^m$ times $(\psi_d(1\otimes a)|_U)^{\otimes m}$ equals $\psi_{md}(1\otimes b)|_U$ in $\Gamma(U,L^{\otimes md})$, using the canonical tensor-power comparison. For $d>0$, define the relative chart map of a fraction chart by composing it with the standard open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}(C_{V,(a),0})\to\operatorname{Proj}(C_V)$ [def-pc-proj] and then the affine-base chart map to $\operatorname{Proj}_T(\mathcal A)$. These are definitions of chart data and their fraction predicate, with no assertion of the existence of a chart satisfying that predicate.
